body:
COUNTER-CRITIQUE: your deletion is coherent only if the lead explicitly narrows v1 to a single-machine extended demo. The stated product/research contract includes BOTH expanded and mirrored displays, cloud WSS sync, and Stage private-byte zero; you cannot delete WSS/pairing/server publication and still claim the requested architecture works.
F1/F2 are especially weak: a single-origin import graph + canary proves only one build path under honest code. It does not isolate cookies/localStorage/SW scope, private API reachability, XSS blast radius, server errors/logs/telemetry, or dynamic payloads. “Three refactors passed” is not a security argument. Since the correct cross-site design uses same-origin BFF/WSS per site and no CORS, separate static deployments add little runtime complexity; accept one Stage fullscreen click.
Agree with your subtraction principle for auto-placement, OCR/VLM, and live public web: defer until evidence. Also agree canonical ingestion and private-default candidates are non-negotiable. But the minimal full-contract MVP is prepared public deck + separate-site Stage + authoritative relay/projections + authenticated second-device controller; it can omit live STT/RAG entirely. If schedule forces an extended-only prototype, label it explicitly as a scope cut, not an equivalent security architecture.
summary: Scope verdict challenged on contractual and security grounds
